why: A retry can only help with a failure that passes.
Trying again is safe only if doing it twice does no more than once.
Stop calling a service that keeps failing, instead of trying it again.
A timeout ends a hung call, so the retry around it can start.
Each step multiplies the last by the same amount.
Doing it again leaves the state where the first time left it.
An idempotent function gives the same result applied once or twice.
The change happens everywhere, or nowhere.
Any party can fail midway, so each first says it can commit.
Others see the state before the change or after it, never between.
Its two sides are sums that must always be equal.
It sets how long to wait between them.
Each wait is a fixed multiple of the last.
Waiting longer each time lowers the load on a service that is struggling.
Stop calling for a while instead of calling less often.
Jitter picks a random wait below the ceiling backoff sets.
The key makes repeating a request idempotent.
The service remembers each key once, and refuses it twice.
A retry sends the same key again, so it can't do the work twice.
A unique key identifies one row and no other.
Holding money is moving it to a held account and back.
First every side agrees, then the change is made.
A call can fail by never answering, which only a time limit can tell.
A limit needs a clock to measure the wait against.
Watch a service's health instead of guessing a time limit.
A transient error is part of a system failing for a while, while the rest goes on.
A transaction's changes happen together or not at all.
A lock taken in a transaction is let go when it ends.
Each entry keeps both sides of the equation equal.
Both entries are written together, or not at all.
The code is a hash of the message mixed with the secret.
Only those who share the secret can make the code.
Checking a code must not leak, through its timing, how much of it matched.
It's needed only when things run at the same time.
Two changes at once can leave shared state inconsistent.
Congestion is more load than a link's bandwidth can carry.
It notices one part failing and stops sending it work for a while.
It keeps a secret from leaking through how long a check takes.
Taking the same time whatever the input leaves nothing to measure.
Only one holder of the lock goes on at a time.
Everything arriving at once is more load than the service can take.
It turns load away before the service is overwhelmed.
